the design and implementation of a real-time FPGA-based 3D image processor that can be used for preprocessing intraoperative volumetric images in IGIs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a reconfigurable architecture that can process large volumetric images at real-time rates and can be programmed with different kernels for different applications.
the proposed FPGA-based architecture can be used for real-time preprocessing (anisotropic diffusion and median filtering) of large intraoperative volumetric images (3D CT, 3D ultrasound) for IGIs.
we have developed a reconfigurable hardware architecture for real-time 3-D image preprocessing that enables the application of these techniques in the I.G.I. workflow prior to advanced processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed architecture is capable of performing 3D image enhancement tasks at a speed comparable to that of 2D image enhancement tasks, while providing the flexibility to implement a variety of 3D image processing algorithms.
